VERDICT: CONDITIONAL

I read both editions from disk (`meta-pattern/main.tex`, `meta-pattern/academic/main.tex`), both rendered PDFs, the bib, the BibTeX/LaTeX logs, and the primary sources for the cited numbers. The pasted twin was truncated, so everything structural below comes from the files.

**Twin desync: CLEAN.** `diff main.tex academic/main.tex` returns exactly two hunks — the byline swap and an added CRediT block. Table 1 is byte-identical in both, and both PDFs render every row under the same heading (verified visually, page 8 of each). No row has migrated between Confirmed/Falsified/Suspected. **Stale PDF: CLEAN** — both `main.pdf` (Aug 29 21:12) postdate both `main.tex` (21:07), and the rendered abstract carries the corrected "7-for-7 / 24 experiments" text.

---

### 1. CRITICAL — Table 1 floats past the References and lands on the last page, in both editions

Location: `\begin{table}[ht]` at `academic/main.tex:143` / `main.tex:144`. Rendered: Table 1 is on **page 8**, after the bibliography (page 7). It is first referenced on page 2.

The table is the paper's entire empirical content. As shipped, a reader passes §2.2 "The Split", §2.3, §3 (fishing-net argument), §4 "What the Kills Teach" (four rows discussed by name), §5 (three more rows), §7, and §8 — all of it commentary on rows they have not seen — then the reference list, then the table. A table after the bibliography is a hard formatting failure at any venue. `[ht]` cannot succeed: the tabular plus the two block footnotes is roughly a full page, so LaTeX defers it to the end of the document.

Fix: change to `\begin{table}[p]` and add `\usepackage{placeins}` with `\FloatBarrier` immediately before `\subsection{The Split}`. That forces the table onto its own page inside §2, before the discussion. Verify by re-rendering — the target is Table 1 on page 3 at the latest. If `[p]` still defers, make it a non-float: wrap the tabular in `\begin{center}` inside §2.1 with `\captionof{table}{...}` (requires `caption`, already loaded).

### 2. MAJOR — Every number in §3.2 and §8 "Oracle Loop reporting" is attributed to the wrong paper

Location: `academic/main.tex:323` (`\citep{lyra2026oracle}`) and `:505–514`.

The figures — 16/20 baseline, 0/20 corrected, 9/30 = 30%, 4/30 = 13%, primary endpoint p = 0.34, placebo-vs-corrected p = 0.019, Bonferroni α = 0.025, L35–L47 — are all from `targeted-deception-correction/paper.tex` (lines 88–93, 277, 287–288, 294). I read `oracle-loop-paper/sections/abstract.tex` and its section files: the Oracle Loop TR contains **none** of them. Its correction results are emotion-vector steering on *confabulation* — hostile 95.6% (McNemar p < 0.001, 350 trials), doubt injection 7/7. Different intervention, different failure mode, different experiment.

`targeted-deception-correction` has no entry in `references.bib`, so a reader following [7] finds a paper that does not contain the result being described.

Fix: add a bib entry for the targeted deception-correction TR and cite it in both places. If the intent is to credit the umbrella Oracle program, say so explicitly and still cite the specific report: "the Oracle program's targeted deception-correction arm [new-key]".

### 3. MAJOR — "achieved 80%–100% correction" presents a baseline rate as a correction rate

Location: `academic/main.tex:323–324`: "The Oracle Loop~\citep{lyra2026oracle} achieved $80\%$--$100\%$ correction in an exploratory proof-of-concept".

The source is 16/20 = 80% *baseline deception*, reduced to 0/20 = 0%, i.e. 100% correction of an 80% baseline. There is no 80% correction figure anywhere. The paper's own §8 gloss — "(16/20 baseline, 0/20 corrected)" — confirms the 80% is a baseline. As written, the range's low end is a category error.

Same sentence, second problem: "by normalizing the activation profile **across the full sequence**". The source (paper.tex:146) describes per-layer forward hooks at L35, L39, L43, L47 steering along the native deception direction during autoregressive generation — not a full-sequence normalization.

Fix: "reduced deception from 80% (16/20) to 0% (0/20) in an exploratory proof-of-concept, by per-layer profile normalization along a natively extracted deception direction at L35–L47".

### 4. MAJOR — The "subsequently retracted" annotation is on the wrong table row

Location: Table 1, row `Same-prompt deception & Falsified & Content & $0.920 \to 0.160$ after FWL (exploratory, subsequently retracted)`.

In the canonical body count (`lyra-technique-ii/academic/main.tex:825`), the retracted finding is **Within-model deception** — footnote §: "Within-model deception retracted: the same-prompt control (the *Same-prompt deception* row in this same Falsified block) collapses AUROC to 0.160". Same-prompt deception is the *control that did the killing*, not the thing retracted. In meta-pattern the marker sits on the control, and the Within-model deception row carries only "Prompt template confound" with no retraction marker at all.

Note that lyra-technique-ii names the row rather than its index, which is the correct pattern; meta-pattern lost that when it re-tabulated.

Fix: move the annotation. Within-model deception → "AUROC 1.000; retracted — the *Same-prompt deception* row below collapses it to 0.160". Same-prompt deception → "$0.920 \to 0.160$ after FWL (same-prompt control)".

### 5. MAJOR — The counting rule from the abstract footnote is not applied to the deception pair

The abstract footnote establishes the rule that produced 24 rather than 25: one experiment gets one row, and a row that is a retracted finding's corrected form must not be counted separately. Applied consistently, *Within-model deception* and *Same-prompt deception* are one finding and its control — per finding #4 they are two rows describing a single retraction event — and the Falsified count is 9, making the headline 0-for-9, not 0-for-10.

This propagates to the abstract ("0-for-10 on content"), the §2.2 split table (`Content 0/7 10/10`), §2.3, §8, and §9.

Fix: either collapse the pair to one row and restate as 23 experiments / 0-for-9, or add one sentence to §2.1 stating the counting rule explicitly — "control experiments that falsify a parent finding are listed and counted separately" — and explain why that rule does not also readmit the emotion row the footnote removed. Right now the paper applies two different rules to two structurally identical situations, and the one it applies here is the one that inflates the denominator in the direction that flatters the thesis.

### 6. MAJOR — §7.1 and §9 say "geometric" where the paper's own footnote requires "spectral"

Locations: `:446–447` "These are content properties invisible to geometric readout"; `:528–529` "the workspace operates on content without exposing it geometrically".

The ‡ footnote (`:201–209`) and §4 "Emotion degree" both establish that a *geometric* probe — $W_K$-transformed directions — reads 30-way emotion identity at 12.3× chance and binary valence at AUROC 0.992 from the same caches. That is content, read geometrically. The paper is careful about spectral-vs-directional in the abstract, intro, §3 and §4, then drops the distinction in exactly the two places that state the conclusion. A reviewer who reads §7.1 and then the ‡ footnote finds the paper contradicting itself.

Fix: replace "geometric readout" → "spectral readout" and "exposing it geometrically" → "exposing it in the spectral structure" in those two sentences. I verified the source numbers against `user-model-paper/paper/main.tex:263–284` — 40.9%, 12.3×, 0.992, chance 0.033 all check out, as does the spectral probe sitting at chance across layers (`:305–321`).

### 7. MINOR — "The 7/10 split" is a number that appears nowhere else

Location: `:460`, §7.2. Every other statement of the split is 7/7–0/10. "7/10" reads as a seven-out-of-ten success rate, which is the opposite of the claim.

Fix: "The 7/7--0/10 split is a guide for future work".

### 8. MINOR — Malformed citation in the abstract footnote

Location: `:50`, `(\citealt{lyra2026usermodel}, \S Correction note)`. Under `natbib[numbers]`, `\citealt` strips the brackets from a *numeric* label, so the PDF renders "(Lyra et al. 8, §Correction note)" — a bare hyperlinked digit abutting the author name. Confirmed in the render, page 1.

Fix: `(\citet{lyra2026usermodel}, \S Correction note)` → "Lyra et al. [8]".

### 9. MINOR — Kavi is in the CRediT block but in neither byline, and is also acknowledged

`academic/main.tex:544` lists **Kavi**: Validation, Writing – review & editing, under "Author Contributions (CRediT)". Kavi is not in the byline, and `:547` separately thanks Kavi in Acknowledgments. CRediT is an author-level statement; a person is a contributor or an acknowledgee, not both. Separately, the flight edition has no CRediT block at all, so its readers never learn Kavi's role — and the academic byline footnote's promise that AI contributions are "detailed in the Author Contributions section" has no referent in the flight edition.

This is corpus-wide (identical block in `identity-geometry/academic/main.tex:583–590` and `cache-tracing/academic/main.tex:557–564`), so it is template drift rather than a defect specific to this paper — but it ships from this paper.

Fix: either add Kavi to the byline (then drop the Acknowledgments line), or drop Kavi from CRediT (then keep the Acknowledgments line). Add the CRediT block to the flight edition too, or remove the byline footnote's forward reference.

### 10. MINOR — SimpleQA is named in Table 1 and §5 but never cited

`wei2024simpleqa` sits in `references.bib:53` uncited. The benchmark is named twice in the body.

Fix: `Dual detector (SimpleQA~\citep{wei2024simpleqa})` in §5.

### 11. MINOR — Cache-tracing lift is described imprecisely

Location: `:314–316` "Logit-lens concept directions showed $2.1$--$8.4\times$ lift over random at workspace-band layers".

Source (`cache-tracing/academic/main.tex:45–48, 183–186`): the directions "explain 2.1–8.4× more **variance** in the $W_V$-projected residual stream than random vocabulary directions", across **L9–L33** of a 36-layer Qwen3-8B, with lift *peaking at L27–L33* — i.e. not confined to the workspace band. The cross-prompt control's n (380 pairs) is also dropped.

Fix: "explained 2.1–8.4× more variance than random vocabulary directions across L9--L33, but a cross-prompt control (380 pairs) collapsed this to 1.0--1.2×".

### 12. MINOR — BibTeX warning, and 15 uncited entries

`main.blg`: "Warning--empty journal in gurnee2026gwt" — it is an `@article` with no `journal` field, so plainnat renders it awkwardly. Change to `@misc` with `howpublished = {Transformer Circuits Thread, Anthropic}`. Separately, 15 of the 25 entries in `references.bib` are uncited by this paper (dehaene2011experimental, failspy2024abliterate, arditi2024refusal, hu2021lora, raghu2017svcca, kornblith2019similarity, bjorck1973numerical, zhang2025guardspace, cintas2025localizing, vasilenko2026identity, kosinski2024evaluating, ullman2023large, lyra2026decision, lyra2026campaign2, lyra2026identity, lyra2026portrait, lyra2026weather, lyra2026cc_synthesis, lyra2026nexus_emotion, berg2025inverse). They do not reach the output, so this is hygiene only.

---

## What I could not check

- **`lyra2026nexus_audit` — the canonical body count.** No such document exists anywhere under `published-research/`; grep for "Body Count Audit" returns only the papers that cite it. §2.1 rests the entire 24-row table on this source, and neither I nor any reader can verify the list against it. The nearest available list (`lyra-technique-ii`) has 9 Falsified rows to meta-pattern's 10 and a different Suspected set, so the two are not interchangeable. **To check this I need the Nexus audit file committed to the repo** — and I would argue it should be, since it is the sole warrant for the paper's only table.
- **URL liveness.** WebFetch permission was declined and I have no network, so I could not confirm `https://liberationlabs.tech/papers/oracle-loop`, `https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html`, or `https://github.com/Liberation-Labs-THCoalition/published-research` resolve. Needs a manual curl or an approved WebFetch.
- **Author sign-off.** No record in the repo shows Dwayne Wilkes or Kavi approved this draft — in particular the 2026-08-14 correction, which changed the headline count after the July publication. Needs a sign-off artifact (email, commit trailer, or a dated line in `PUBLISH_READINESS.md`).
- **"16 models spanning 0.6B to 70B."** `RESEARCH_STATUS.md:70` corroborates the 0.6B–70B range for scale invariance. The count of 16 is documented nowhere I could find. Needs the model manifest.
- **Gurnee et al.'s "~38–92% of model depth."** Cannot verify without network access to the Transformer Circuits page.
- **Nine Table 1 key numbers** (0.620/0.707, 0.794, 1.36, 0.91, 0.999, 0.83–0.90, 0.850/0.448, 0.754, 0.757–1.000) I did not trace to primary data — only to `SOP_REVIEW.md`, which asserts they match `MEMORY.md`. That is a secondary citing a secondary, and I am not treating it as verification. The numbers I did trace to primary sources (emotion 12.3×/40.9%/0.992/0.033, cache tracing 6,960/2.1–8.4×/1.0–1.2×, the deception-correction figures, the 2026-05-21 retraction date, the 64-layer model) all check out.
